check: Verify that switching between folded cover screen and unfolded inner screen preserves form state, scroll position, and recalculates split-pane layouts without reload.
why_forgotten: Standard viewport resize tests rarely simulate mid-interaction aspect-ratio jumps on stateful B2B order forms.

check: Verify that hardware barcode scanners emitting rapid keystrokes plus Enter/Tab in warehouse views append/increment items without triggering premature form submission or losing input focus.
why_forgotten: Developers test with physical keyboards and mice rather than rugged Zebra/Honeywell terminals.

check: Verify that opening the on-screen numeric keypad on tablets and phones does not hide sticky 'Submit Order' bars or active quantity inputs inside scrollable tables.
why_forgotten: Headless desktop browser emulation does not trigger mobile OS `visualViewport` shrinkage from soft keyboards.

check: Verify that warehouse packing actions avoid hover-only menus, drag-and-drop without tap alternatives, or tightly packed destructive buttons under `@media (pointer: coarse)`.
why_forgotten: AI agents default to desktop-first UI component patterns that rely on precise cursor interaction.

check: Verify that inline editing of quantities in a 200-row B2B quick-order table preserves logical Tab/Arrow key navigation and does not reset focus to `document.body` after async price recalculation.
why_forgotten: Axe static scans pass even when React/Vue state re-renders destroy active DOM nodes and drop keyboard focus.

check: Verify that background stock warnings, credit-limit alerts, and toast notifications use appropriate `aria-live` polite/assertive regions and are announced by screen readers.
why_forgotten: Visual diff and static DOM checks only inspect mounted states, missing ephemeral toast lifecycle semantics.

check: Verify that multi-step filter drawers, Tpay payment modals, and confirmation dialogs trap Tab focus inside and restore focus to the trigger element on Escape.
why_forgotten: Custom or nested portals created by coding agents frequently break focus-trap layering.

check: Verify that an order containing 500+ distinct SKU lines remains responsive (<100ms INP) during quantity edits via row virtualization or memoized state updates.
why_forgotten: Synthetic tests use 2-3 sample cart items, whereas B2B wholesale buyers order hundreds of SKUs at once.

check: Verify that catalog listings with customer-specific price tiers, discounts, and multi-warehouse stock levels execute in bounded SQL queries rather than per-SKU lookups.
why_forgotten: ORM lazy-loading works fast on tiny seed databases in CI but collapses under production catalog sizes.

check: Verify that warehouse and sales rep dashboards kept open for an 8-hour shift do not leak heap memory through detached DOM nodes, polling intervals, or WebSocket listeners.
why_forgotten: E2E tests open a page for seconds, never simulating an all-day work shift.

check: Verify that manipulating order IDs, invoice IDs, or delivery address IDs in API payloads cannot read or mutate records belonging to another B2B customer or unassigned sales region.
why_forgotten: AI agents often check `isAuthenticated` and role names while forgetting row-level ownership predicates in queries.

check: Verify that user-supplied fields (company name, delivery notes, SKU comments) starting with `=`, `+`, `-`, or `@` are neutralized before generating XLSX exports for accountants or ERP import.
why_forgotten: Teams treat XLSX generation as safe binary output, forgetting Excel executes formulas when accountants open the file.

check: Verify that payment callback endpoints validate Tpay JWS/MD5 signatures against trusted certificates, enforce IP allowlists if applicable, and reject replayed transaction notifications.
why_forgotten: Sandbox payment testing focuses on the happy-path redirect rather than adversarial webhook spoofing.

check: Verify that customer and warehouse API responses strip sensitive fields like wholesale purchase cost, merchant margin, customer credit score, and internal sales rep notes.
why_forgotten: Backend endpoints frequently serialize entire ORM entities and rely on the frontend UI to hide restricted columns.

check: Verify that a customer patching their cart or profile cannot overwrite protected attributes such as `discountPercent`, `creditLimit`, `paymentTermsDays`, or `assignedSalesRepId`.
why_forgotten: Auto-generated DTOs or permissive schema validators often bind all model fields by default.

item: Tax retention vs right to erasure
check: Verify that GDPR account deletion anonymizes personal contact data while preserving immutable invoice, NIP, and order ledger records required for 5+ years by Polish tax law.
why_forgotten: Naive `ON DELETE CASCADE` or full-row wiping violates Polish accounting regulations (Ustawa o rachunkowości).

check: Verify that when an admin or sales rep places or edits an order on behalf of a customer, an immutable audit log records both the actor identity and the target customer account.
why_forgotten: Impersonation is often implemented by swapping session tokens without preserving the original `actor_id`.

item: PII leakage in logs and telemetry
check: Verify that application logs, Sentry breadcrumbs, and error payloads scrub NIP, PESEL, customer emails, passwords, street addresses, and session tokens before ingestion.
why_forgotten: Full request body logging is turned on for debugging ERP/payment issues and left active in production.

check: Verify that production database snapshots restored to staging or preview environments scrub real customer emails and phone numbers so test runs cannot email real B2B clients.
why_forgotten: Developers copy production data to debug Example ERP sync edge cases without sanitizing notification targets.

check: Verify that sorting customer names, cities, and products uses `Intl.Collator('pl')` or PostgreSQL `pl_PL.utf8` collation so `Łódź` sorts after `Lublin` rather than at the end of Z.
why_forgotten: Default ASCII/UTF-8 code-point sorting places Polish characters (`ą, ć, ę, ł, ń, ó, ś, ź, ż`) after `z`.

check: Verify that searching `ladowarka` or `zolty` matches `Ładowarka` and `Żółty`, and Unicode normalization (NFC vs macOS NFD) does not break SKU or customer lookups.
why_forgotten: Standard SQL `ILIKE` is accent-sensitive unless `unaccent` or normalized search tokens are configured.

item: Polish numeric and currency input parsing
check: Verify that price and decimal quantity inputs accept both comma (`12,50`) and dot (`12.50`), format currency as `1 234,56 zł` with non-breaking spaces, and never truncate after a comma.
why_forgotten: `parseFloat('12,50')` silently returns `12` in JavaScript if comma normalization is omitted.

check: Verify that UI counters use all three Polish plural forms (1 sztuka, 2-4 sztuki, 5-21 sztuk, 22 sztuki) rather than English singular/plural logic.
why_forgotten: AI agents trained primarily on English codebases often hardcode `count === 1 ? 'produkt' : 'produkty'`.

check: Verify that daily order cutoffs, invoice issue dates, and ERP sync windows around the March/October CET-to-CEST transition do not shift by an hour or duplicate daily reports.
why_forgotten: Naive UTC midnight arithmetic (`+ 86400s`) breaks twice a year in local Polish business time.

check: Verify that generated XLSX files use explicit numeric/currency cell types (not strings) and any CSV fallbacks include UTF-8 BOM and semicolon (`;`) delimiters so Polish Excel opens diacritics and columns cleanly.
why_forgotten: Default UTF-8 CSVs with comma delimiters open as garbled single-column text in Polish Windows Excel.

check: Verify that transactional order emails with large SKU tables render cleanly in classic Windows Outlook (Word rendering engine) without broken flexbox/grid layouts or clipped totals.
why_forgotten: Modern browser previews render CSS Grid/Flexbox fine, whereas corporate B2B clients use desktop Outlook.

item: Large attachment limit and bounce fallback
check: Verify that when an order XLSX exceeds corporate SMTP/Exchange limits (e.g., >10MB), the system falls back to a time-limited authenticated download link and alerts on hard bounces.
why_forgotten: Test orders have tiny attachments that never trigger SMTP size rejection or recipient mailbox quotas.

check: Verify that outbound emails pass SPF, DKIM, and DMARC alignment, include proper `List-Unsubscribe` headers where appropriate, and process bounce/complaint webhooks.
why_forgotten: Application tests only check that the SMTP client returned `250 OK`, not whether messages land in spam.

item: Multi-page print stylesheet and page breaks
check: Verify that printing warehouse pick-lists or proforma invoices via `@media print` repeats `<thead>` on every page, prevents splitting table rows or summary blocks, and hides navigation chrome.
why_forgotten: UX device matrices test screen viewports but skip browser print preview and physical pagination.

item: PDF Polish font embedding and barcodes
check: Verify that server-generated PDFs embed full Latin-Extended glyphs for `ąęćłńóśźż` and render high-contrast vector barcodes/QR codes readable by laser scanners after grayscale printing.
why_forgotten: Default PDF fonts (Helvetica/Times) in headless generators drop Polish glyphs or render blurry raster barcodes.

check: Verify that non-production environments emit `X-Robots-Tag: noindex`, private B2B endpoints return 401/403 instead of soft-200 login pages, and public catalog pages have valid canonical/sitemap tags.
why_forgotten: SPAs often return HTTP 200 for all routes, causing search engines to index empty shell pages or staging hosts.

check: Verify that orders placed or browsed by sales reps/admins in customer-impersonation mode are tagged separately and do not skew customer conversion funnels or GA4/PostHog metrics.
why_forgotten: Client-side analytics snippets fire indiscriminately on every pageview regardless of actor session type.

check: Verify that critical B2B funnel telemetry (order submission, payment initiation, ERP export failure) is recorded server-side or via first-party proxy so corporate adblockers do not blind ops.
why_forgotten: QA browsers run clean profiles without uBlock Origin or strict corporate DNS filters.

check: Verify that when a new release invalidates lazy-loaded JS/CSS hashes while a user has the app open, the client catches `ChunkLoadError` and gracefully reloads or prompts without a blank screen.
why_forgotten: Single-version test runs never simulate mid-session asset eviction during continuous deployment.

item: Dead-letter queue and silent async failure alerts
check: Verify that failed background jobs (Example ERP sync, XLSX email dispatch, Tpay status reconciliation) trigger high-priority alerts and surface a visible retry state in the admin panel.
why_forgotten: Unhandled promise rejections are caught in Sentry, while exhausted BullMQ/Sidekiq retries fail silently in Redis.

check: Verify on a schedule that encrypted database and object-storage backups can be restored into an isolated instance and pass an integrity query check within the target RTO.
why_forgotten: Teams verify that the backup cron job exits 0, but never test if `pg_restore` succeeds or if attachments are included.

check: Verify that database migrations do not rename/drop columns or acquire long `ACCESS EXCLUSIVE` locks while the previous application version and background workers are still running.
why_forgotten: In CI, migrations run before starting a single server instance, masking rolling-deploy version skew.

check: Verify that queued Redis/worker payloads enqueued before a deploy can still be deserialized and processed by new worker code (or rolled-back worker code).
why_forgotten: Developers change job payload schemas alongside producer code, forgetting already-queued jobs in production.

check: Verify that XLSX generation, PDF invoice rendering, and complex catalog filtering enforce per-user and per-tenant concurrency/rate limits to prevent accidental DoS.
why_forgotten: Rate limiting is usually applied only to `/login`, leaving expensive authenticated B2B endpoints unprotected.

item: Credential stuffing and OTP brute-force protection
check: Verify that login, password reset, and NIP lookup endpoints enforce progressive backoff or per-account lockouts without allowing an attacker to lock out legitimate B2B admins globally.
why_forgotten: IP-only rate limits either fail behind shared corporate NATs or get bypassed by distributed botnets.

item: Outdated Android WebView on warehouse devices
check: Verify that JS bundles and CSS features (e.g., `:has()`, container queries, modern array methods) transpile or degrade gracefully on older Chromium WebViews locked on industrial Android scanners.
why_forgotten: Playwright runs the latest evergreen Chromium, whereas warehouse hardware often runs 3-year-old Android OS builds.

item: Safari ITP and strict cookie partitioning
check: Verify that authentication, Tpay return redirects, and embedded previews work on iOS/macOS Safari without relying on blocked third-party cookies or fragile `SameSite=None` flows.
why_forgotten: Developers on Linux/Windows test WebKit via Playwright on Linux, which lacks full Apple ITP behavior.

check: Verify that service workers never serve cached catalog prices, stock availability, or customer credit limits via `CacheFirst` strategies, and immediately activate updates on financial routes.
why_forgotten: PWA boilerplates aggressively cache API responses to pass offline audits, causing customers to order at outdated prices.

check: Verify that when a sales rep builds an order offline and reconnects after prices or stock changed on the server, the app highlights diffs for confirmation instead of silently submitting or discarding the draft.
why_forgotten: Offline checks usually only test whether an offline banner appears, not the state reconciliation upon reconnect.

check: Verify that retrying a partially failed order workflow does not send duplicate order-confirmation XLSX emails to the customer or duplicate pick requests to the warehouse.
why_forgotten: Email dispatch is often placed inside the same non-idempotent job step as ERP synchronization.

item: KSeF schema, token renewal, and offline24 mode
check: Verify that structured e-invoices validate against the current Ministry of Finance `FA(2)`/`FA(3)` XSD, handle KSeF session/token expiration, and support the mandatory offline/contingency issuance flow during KSeF maintenance.
why_forgotten: Teams only test happy-path XML generation against the KSeF demo API, ignoring KSeF downtime laws and schema edge cases.

item: NIP checksum, GUS/VIES, and Biała Lista VAT
check: Verify that B2B onboarding and invoicing validate the modulo-11 NIP checksum, handle prefixed EU VAT numbers, and verify active VAT status / bank accounts against the MF White List API.
why_forgotten: AI agents often validate NIP as a mere 10-digit regex `/^\d{10}$/` without checksum or ministry registry checks.

item: Versioned Regulamin acceptance and Cookie Consent
check: Verify that B2B terms of service (`Regulamin`) updates require explicit re-acceptance with timestamped audit proof, and non-essential analytics cookies do not fire prior to consent.
why_forgotten: A simple boolean `terms_accepted = true` column loses track of which legal version the customer agreed to.

check: Verify that a single `trace_id`/`correlation_id` flows from the browser request through API logs, async queue jobs, Example ERP sync calls, and Tpay webhooks.
why_forgotten: Async boundaries (message queues and incoming webhooks) drop HTTP context headers unless explicitly propagated.

check: Verify that monitoring alerts trigger when business metrics flatline during Polish working hours (e.g., 0 orders placed, 0 ExampleERP syncs completed, or >15% Tpay abandonment spike in 1 hour).
why_forgotten: Infrastructure alerts only watch CPU/5xx errors, missing silent logical deadlocks that return HTTP 200.

item: Line-level vs header-level VAT rounding parity
check: Verify that net-to-gross and VAT (23%, 8%, 5%, 0%, zw.) calculations use exact decimal arithmetic (`grosze` integers or `Decimal`) and match Example ERP's exact rounding method to the grosz.
why_forgotten: JavaScript floating-point math or mismatched per-line vs per-rate VAT summation causes 0,01 zł discrepancies rejected by ExampleERP/KSeF.

item: Idempotent order submission and payment initiation
check: Verify that double-clicking 'Order and Pay' or retrying on a flaky mobile connection with an `Idempotency-Key` creates exactly one order, one stock reservation, and one Tpay transaction.
why_forgotten: Frontend button disabling (`disabled={loading}`) is bypassed by network retries or rapid touch events.

item: Credit limit and stock reservation race conditions
check: Verify that concurrent orders from the same customer account cannot exceed their B2B credit limit or oversell the last warehouse unit due to missing `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` or atomic locks.
why_forgotten: Sequential integration tests never execute simultaneous checkout transactions in parallel.

check: Verify across the full matrix (Admin, Accountant, Warehouse, Sales Rep, Customer) that each role can only trigger permitted order status transitions (e.g., Warehouse cannot mark an unpaid non-credit order as settled).
why_forgotten: Permission checks guard route access (`canEditOrder`) rather than validating the specific state machine transition per role.

item: Immediate revocation on role change or block
check: Verify that deactivating a sales rep or blocking a delinquent B2B customer immediately invalidates active JWTs/sessions and rejects in-flight API mutations without waiting for token expiry.
why_forgotten: Stateless JWT authentication continues to grant access until expiration unless a revocation check is enforced.

check: Verify that if a sales rep adjusts discounts on an order while the customer simultaneously edits quantities, optimistic locking (`version` / `ETag`) prevents silent lost updates.
why_forgotten: Single-user E2E flows never simulate two different roles editing the same order entity at the same time.

item: Example ERP lock and partial-sync recovery
check: Verify that when Example ERP's SQL database or API is locked by an accountant running month-end closing, the integration queues orders with exponential backoff, avoids duplicate contractors/documents on retry, and surfaces sync lag in the UI.
why_forgotten: Mocked ERP tests in CI return instant 200 responses, ignoring real-world ExampleERP database locks and non-atomic batch imports.
